cards.name: Shadows/Highlights
cards.summary: Locally brightens dark areas (Shadow amount 35% by default) and, once the Highlight amount is raised from its default 0, darkens bright areas, judging each pixel against its neighbourhood (radius) rather than applying one global curve, so a backlit or underexposed subject opens up without washing out the rest of the frame. Overdone it looks flat, grey and HDR-like, with glowing halos along high-contrast edges.
use_for: opening up dark clothing and shadows in a press or event photo before it goes on a news card
rescuing a backlit portrait shot against a window or bright sky
pulling detail back into a blown wall, shirt or sky with the Highlight amount
evening out a harshly lit product or interior shot before colour grading
avoid: a small radius with a large amount: grey halos and outlines appear along edges; raise the radius or lower the amount
a plain global brighten or darken: Curves or Levels is simpler and keeps contrast
deep, noisy shadows: lifting them shows noise and compression blocks (very visible on a soft video frame); run Reduce Noise after
it is a destructive menu command on a pixel layer and has no adjustment layer: convert the layer to a Smart Object first to keep it editable

scripts: the main controls (Shadow and Highlight amount / width / radius) are object params and must be sent as an adaptCorrectTones descriptor; demo_settings cannot carry them, so the gallery frame relies on the shadow lift Photoshop applied with nothing specified in the harvest read-back (35%, Highlight 0)

params.name: Shadow
params.does: adaptCorrectTones object: amount (% lift of the shadows, default 35), width (% of the tonal range treated as shadow, default 50), radius (neighbourhood size in px, default 30) that decides what counts as a dark area
params.typical: amount 25-50%, width 30-50%, radius 30-100 px (bigger on large images for smoother transitions)

params.name: Highlight
params.does: adaptCorrectTones object with the same amount / width / radius fields, darkening the brightest areas; amount defaults to 0 (off)
params.typical: amount 10-30% to recover a bright wall, shirt or window; 0 when only shadows need help

params.name: center
params.does: contrast of the midtones after the correction (the dialog's Midtone Contrast); positive values put back the punch that lifting shadows removes

params.name: Color Correction
params.does: saturation of the corrected areas only, so lifted shadows do not go grey or over-colourful
params.typical: +20 (default) to +40; lower if lifted skin turns orange

params.name: Black Clip
params.does: percentage of the darkest pixels clipped to pure black after the correction

params.name: White Clip
params.does: percentage of the brightest pixels clipped to pure white after the correction

params.name: Brightness
params.does: declared in Photoshop's terminology with no default; believed to be the slider shown in place of Color Correction on grayscale images (not confirmed by the harvest)

pairs_with: Curves or Levels (set final contrast after the lift)
Reduce Noise (cleans the noise the lift exposes)
Vibrance (restores colour in the opened-up areas)
Convert for Smart Filters (keeps it editable)
cards.scripting: var s = new ActionDescriptor(); s.putUnitDouble(stringIDToTypeID("amount"), stringIDToTypeID("percentUnit"), 50); s.putUnitDouble(stringIDToTypeID("width"), stringIDToTypeID("percentUnit"), 50); s.putInteger(stringIDToTypeID("radius"), 30); var h = new ActionDescriptor(); h.putUnitDouble(stringIDToTypeID("amount"), stringIDToTypeID("percentUnit"), 15); h.putUnitDouble(stringIDToTypeID("width"), stringIDToTypeID("percentUnit"), 50); h.putInteger(stringIDToTypeID("radius"), 30); var d = new ActionDescriptor(); d.putObject(stringIDToTypeID("shadowMode"), stringIDToTypeID("adaptCorrectTones"), s); d.putObject(stringIDToTypeID("highlightMode"), stringIDToTypeID("adaptCorrectTones"), h); d.putDouble(stringIDToTypeID("blackClip"), 0.01); d.putDouble(stringIDToTypeID("whiteClip"), 0.01); d.putInteger(stringIDToTypeID("center"), 30); d.putInteger(stringIDToTypeID("colorCorrection"), 40); executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("adaptCorrect"), d, DialogModes.NO);  // keys and the adaptCorrectTones layout are from the harvest read-back; the harvest found no clamp on blackClip / whiteClip / center / colorCorrection, so keep them in the dialog's ranges
cards.non_destructive: no on a pixel layer (harvest: destructive menu command, and there is no Shadows/Highlights adjustment layer); applied to a Smart Object it becomes an editable Smart Filter
cards.cost: medium: a radius-based local tone pass; large radius values on big images take noticeably longer than a global adjustment

review.changes: summary: highlights are only darkened once Highlight amount is raised (harvested default 0); demo_settings: dropped center 30 (Midtone Contrast +30 pushes the lifted lower midtones back down, working against the only visible change, the default 35% shadow lift, and against the card's 'low contrast' look), kept colorCorrection 40; equivalents.CDR: Bitmaps/Image Adjustment Lab (a multi-adjust dialog, mapped to Camera Raw Filter) -> Effects/Adjust/Light (SMHEffect: the dedicated Shadows / Midtones / Highlights band effect, scriptable, still global not local); avoid: reworded the gallery-default note

verified.note: Shadows open up (ramp 5/63 to 14/99, dark areas lifted) and the frame flattens, from the default Shadow amount 35%; Color Correction 40 adds a little colour; matches the summary.

cards.name: Threshold
cards.summary: Turns the image into pure black and white: every pixel brighter than the Level becomes white, every darker pixel becomes black, with no greys or colour left. The result is a stark, stencil or photocopy look with hard, jagged edges.
use_for: a stencil or street-art poster portrait from a photo
screen-print or one-colour artwork prepared from a photo
cleaning a scanned signature, stamp or line drawing to solid black on white before tracing
finding the darkest and lightest points of an image (slide the Level to the ends) before setting Curves or Levels
avoid: a soft or low-contrast photo (like a video frame) breaks into blotchy shapes: raise contrast or sharpen first, or blur slightly to smooth the edge
two colours other than black and white: use Gradient Map, or Threshold followed by a colour fill in a blend mode
keeping some midtones: use Posterize for a few levels instead of one cut
it is a destructive menu command: use a Threshold adjustment layer to keep the Level editable

params.name: Level
params.does: the cut-off brightness (1-255): pixels brighter than it go white, darker ones go black; higher values make more of the image black
params.typical: 110-150 for a balanced portrait; 128 is the default

pairs_with: Gaussian Blur or Median before it (smoother, less noisy edges)
Brightness/Contrast or Curves before it (decides what falls on each side of the cut)
Image Trace in Illustrator (turns the result into vector shapes)
cards.scripting: var d = new ActionDescriptor(); d.putInteger(stringIDToTypeID("level"), 140); executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("thresholdClassEvent"), d, DialogModes.NO);  // level is clamped by Photoshop to 1..255
cards.non_destructive: no: the Image > Adjustments command rewrites the pixel layer (harvest: destructive); a Threshold adjustment layer gives the same result editable

verified.note: Pure black and white at Level 140: hard stencil edges, the yellow and orange blocks white and the rest black.

cards.name: Vibrance
cards.summary: Raises (or lowers) colour intensity selectively: the Vibrance slider pushes muted colours more than already saturated ones and is designed to hold back skin tones; the Saturation slider beside it changes every colour by the same amount. It is not clip-proof: on the photo plate, whose colours are almost all muted warm tones, Vibrance 100 with Saturation 25 drives the whole frame to near-full saturation (the tan wall turns saturated yellow-orange and the blue channel collapses). Negative Vibrance mutes the dull colours first, for a soft, faded look.
use_for: making a dull event or travel photo look richer while keeping faces natural
boosting a flat, washed-out video frame before it goes into a social post
a muted, pastel or faded editorial grade (negative Vibrance)
matching colour intensity of photos placed side by side in a collage
avoid: colours that are already saturated (logos, strong reds, the colour strip) change less with Vibrance alone; with Saturation added (25 in the gallery frame) the strip's blocks were pushed to full saturation too, so use Saturation or Hue/Saturation when everything must shift
high Saturation values clip bright reds and oranges into flat blobs; keep Saturation modest and let Vibrance do the work
full black and white: use Black & White or Desaturate, not Vibrance at -100

it is a destructive menu command: the editable version is the Color and vibrance adjustment layer (Layer > New Adjustment Layer > Color and vibrance, the former Vibrance layer, which adds Temperature and Tint)
scripts: the harvest read back no default or range for vibrance / saturation (declared integer keys only, so pass both); Adobe documents the dialog sliders as -100..+100, not probed in this version
high Vibrance on an image made mostly of muted warm tones still clips it, worse with Saturation added: raise it gradually and watch the blue channel

params.name: Vibrance
params.does: smart saturation: boosts low-saturation colours most and protects skin tones; negative values mute the dullest colours first
params.typical: +30 to +60 for a natural boost; -30 to -60 for a faded look

params.name: Saturation
params.does: uniform saturation change for all colours, like Hue/Saturation's Saturation

pairs_with: Shadows/Highlights or Curves (fix tone first, then colour)
Camera Raw Filter (has the same Vibrance control)
cards.scripting: var d = new ActionDescriptor(); d.putInteger(stringIDToTypeID("vibrance"), 100); d.putInteger(stringIDToTypeID("saturation"), 25); executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("vibrance"), d, DialogModes.NO);  // both keys are declared integers; no default or clamp was read back, keep them in the documented -100..+100
cards.non_destructive: no: the Image > Adjustments command rewrites the pixel layer (harvest: destructive); the Color and vibrance adjustment layer (adjustmentLayer:vibrance) gives the same result editable

review.changes: avoid + non_destructive: the editable version in 27.4 is the 'Color and vibrance' adjustment layer (Layer/New Adjustment Layer/Color and vibrance, id adjustmentLayer:vibrance), not a 'Vibrance adjustment layer'; marked the -100..+100 range as Adobe documentation, not harvested

verified.note: Vibrance 100 + Saturation 25 drive the warm, muted photo to near-full saturation: the tan wall turns saturated yellow-orange, the photo's blue channel collapses (mean 70 to 13) and 66 % of its pixels end with a clipped channel (0.8 % on the plate), and the colour blocks also go to full saturation; the claim "richer without neon clipping" is not borne out. Summary and the first avoid line rewritten.

second_opinion.note: Re-measured clipping on the photo area (0.8 % to 66 % of pixels with a 0 or 255 channel) and the blue-channel collapse; the plate is mostly muted warm tones, which is exactly where Vibrance acts hardest, so the frame is a fair test of the overclaim, not a plate artefact. The rewrite keeps the slider description and drops "without neon clipping".
